title: How to Create Order Presets in TradingView, Save Risk to Reward Easily 2026
description:
Here I will show you How to Create Order Presets in TradingView, Save Risk to Reward Easily 2026 

In this video, I'll guide you on how to create order presets in TradingView, an essential feature to streamline your trading process. Whether you're a beginner or experienced with TradingView, setting up order presets can significantly enhance your efficiency, allowing you to focus more on your trading strategy.

Start by navigating to tradingview.com and signing into your account. Once logged in, open a chart you plan to work with, as this is where you'll begin configuring your order presets. Having the chart visible allows you to see your adjustments in real-time, providing a visual guide to your preset settings.

At the lower part of your screen, click on the trade button to open the trading panel for your selected chart. This panel is crucial for defining the specifics of your trading orders, so it's important to become familiar with navigating it. Within the trading panel, find the option to adjust the market units, allowing you to specify the number of units for your order. This step is akin to setting the scale of your trade, tailored to your investment goals and market analysis.

Next, manage your risk settings, a vital step in determining the financial exposure you're willing to accept in a trade. Carefully adjust these settings to align with your risk tolerance and trading strategy. Effective risk management is key to sustainable trading success, so take your time with this step.

After adjusting your risk settings, analyze the profit and loss projections to ensure they align with your financial objectives. If anything seems off, make the necessary adjustments here to maintain a balance between potential returns and acceptable risk levels.

Once the key components of your order are configured, click on the save order preset option. This step consolidates all your custom settings into a reusable template, saving you from manually inputting the same parameters for similar trades. Choose a name for your order preset that reflects its purpose or trade strategy, aiding in quick identification and application in the future.

Finally, confirm your inputs by clicking save. Your order preset is now ready for use in future trades, ensuring consistency and speed in executing your trading strategy. Remember, you can edit these presets anytime your trading strategy evolves."

title: How to Create Horizontal Scrolling Images in Squarespace 2026, with Auto Play & Thumbnails
description:
Here I will show you How to Create Horizontal Scrolling Images in Squarespace 2026, with Auto Play & Thumbnails.

"In today's video, I'm going to teach you **how to create horizontal scrolling images in Squarespace**. If you've ever wondered how to make your website more dynamic and visually stimulating, adding a horizontal scrolling image gallery could be the perfect touch. It's an excellent way to display your portfolio, feature products, or share any collection of images in an interactive and engaging format. Let's dive right into this simple and effective process.
 

 First off, you'll need to log into your Squarespace account. On the login page, click the login button and select ""Continue with Google"" to swiftly sign in using your existing Google credentials. Once logged in, you'll be directed to your dashboard, where you'll see a list of your existing websites. Click on the website you plan to modify or add images to, which will open the editing interface tailored to your particular site.
 

 Now, let's move to the editing process. Start by navigating to the edit option on your Squarespace menu. Once you've opened the editing tools, your next step is to add a new section. Click on ""Add Section"" in your page editor to access a variety of customizable sections. To include images, click on the ""Images"" tab. This feature is your gateway to creating a new scrolling gallery.
 

 Select ""Gallery View"" from the available options to ensure your images are organized in an attractive and accessible format. Moving forward, click on ""Edit Section"" to fine-tune the settings of your image gallery. In the editing options, navigate to the ""Grid"" simple dropdown. From this menu, choose ""Slideshow Simple."" This setting will transform your grid layout into a sleek slideshow format perfect for horizontal scrolling.
 

 Next, enhance the functionality of your gallery by turning on the thumbnails option. Thumbnails provide a preview of each image, allowing visitors to browse through your gallery quickly and efficiently. To make your gallery truly come to life, click on the autoplay option. Enabling autoplay ensures your slideshow progresses automatically, without needing manual navigation from your website visitors.
 

 Lastly, to ensure the pacing of your slideshow suits your audience, scale down the slide duration to keep the experience engaging. Adjusting the duration helps create a delightful viewing rhythm that enhances the visitor experience.
 

 And there you have it! You've successfully created a horizontally scrolling image gallery on your Squarespace site. This captivating feature not only adds a dynamic visual element to your site but also enriches how your audience engages with your content. Thanks for watching, and happy creating!"

title: How to Fix Squarespace This rule is conflicting with an existing DNS record while Domain Forwarding
description:
Here is How to Fix Squarespace This rule is conflicting with an existing DNS record while Domain Forwarding. 

In this video, I’ll show you how to fix a common issue that pops up when setting up domain forwarding in Squarespace — specifically when you're trying to add a forwarding rule using the built-in Forwarding feature.

Many users see this error message:

“This rule is conflicting with an existing DNS record. Resolve by deleting the conflicting record in the DNS settings page.”

This can be confusing, but don’t worry — I’ll walk you through exactly how to fix it.

Let’s break down what’s actually happening.

When you try to forward a subdomain — like www.pmntechfix.nl — Squarespace checks if there are existing DNS records already set for that subdomain. If there’s an A record, CNAME, or any custom record tied to that subdomain, Squarespace won’t let you add a forwarding rule until you remove the conflict.

And that’s what triggers the error message.

Now here’s how to fix it:

Step 1: Go to your DNS Settings.

On the left panel, click Settings, then select Domains, and choose your domain — for example, pmntechfix.nl.

Next, scroll down and click on DNS Settings.

Here, you’ll see a full list of DNS records associated with your domain. Look for any existing CNAME or A records under the subdomain you were trying to forward — in most cases, it’s the www record.

Step 2: Delete the conflicting record.

To do that, simply click the trash icon next to that DNS entry. This tells Squarespace to remove its current mapping — so it no longer points the subdomain to an old destination.

(insert video showing deletion of the conflicting DNS record here)

Once the record is deleted, go back to your Forwarding settings, and try adding the rule again — this time it should work without any errors.

Quick Note:
If you’re forwarding your root domain (with @ as the subdomain), you might need to remove multiple conflicting A records — usually the default Squarespace ones. Don’t worry — once forwarding is active, you won’t need those A records anymore.

And that’s it!
You’ve successfully fixed the domain forwarding conflict in Squarespace.

If this helped, don’t forget to like the video, subscribe to the channel, and let me know in the comments if you're still stuck.

Thanks for watching, and I’ll see you in the next one.
